title: TEM Analysis of Fe-Doped ZnAl Hydrotalcite (ZnAl-LDH/Fe3O4) for Enhanced Photocatalytic Reduction of Cr VI in Water
content: Layered double hydroxides (LDH) also known as hydrotalcites (HT) are materials with a structure formed by positively charged layers that form a three-dimensional network (bimetallic or trimetallic) [1,2]. They are characterized by having a high surface area and active structure, making them very useful in areas of catalysis and photocatalysis [3]. LDHs present the interesting capacity of tuning their properties by introducing ions into their structure. On the other hand, Fe incorporation has been reported to generate defects that improve optical properties, promote charge separation and modify the electronic structure in HDLs (particularly in ZnAl-LDH), allowing a better performance in oxidation or reduction reactions for photocatalytic processes [4], as the mineralization of organic compounds and the reduction of heavy metal as hexavalent chromium Cr(VI) [5] present as pollutants in aqueous sources. As an important tool to explain the above mentioned properties of LDH, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was employed to analyze the morphology of ZnAl-LDH/Fe3O4 photocatalyst, used as an effective photocatalyst to remove Cr(VI) from water.
